grammar_details.focus: Present Perfect Tense (have/has + V3) with for/since & Quantifiers

rules.usage: Actions occurring at an unspecified time before now, or actions beginning in the past and continuing into the present.
examples: I have studied English for three years.
She has lived in Shiraz since 1395.

rules.formula: for + duration of time (for two hours, for ten years)  |  since + starting point in time (since yesterday, since 1400)
examples: They have practiced sign language for months.
He has been interested in foreign languages since childhood.

rules.structure: Quantifiers with Countable vs Uncountable Nouns
rules.formula: many / a few + countable plural nouns  |  much / a little + uncountable nouns  |  a lot of + both
examples: There are many languages in the world.
We need a little time to translate this text.

writing_skills.topic: Gerunds (V-ing) as Sentence Subjects & Word Formation
rules: A gerund (V-ing) can function as the subject of a sentence and takes a singular verb.
Example: 'Learning a foreign language (S) opens (V) new doors to world cultures.'
Example: 'Communicating with deaf people requires sign language.'

vocab_development.rules: Suffix -ly converts adjectives into adverbs of manner (fluent -> fluently, natural -> naturally, easy -> easily, quick -> quickly). Prefix re- means 'again' (read -> reread, write -> rewrite, build -> rebuild, play -> replay).
examples: fluent -> fluently
write -> rewrite
build -> rebuild

see_also.rules: Pronunciation of have/has contractions ('ve, 's, haven't, hasn't). When a word ending in a consonant sound is followed by a word beginning with a vowel, the consonant links to the vowel.

lessons.title: A Healthy Lifestyle
lessons.theme: Physical health, nutrition, stress, exercise, prevention

grammar_details.focus: Gerunds & Infinitives and Conditional Sentences Type 1

rules.formula: verb + V-ing (enjoy, avoid, practice, mind, finish)  |  verb + to + base verb (decide, hope, plan, promise, want)
examples: You should avoid eating fast food.
She decided to exercise every morning.

rules.formula: If + Simple Present (condition), will / can / may + base verb (result)
rules.usage: Real or very likely future conditions and their probable results.
examples: If you eat a balanced diet, you will stay energetic and healthy.
If students manage their daily stress, they can perform better in exams.

writing_skills.topic: The Three Essential Parts of a Paragraph
rules: A paragraph is a group of sentences about a single main idea.
1. Topic Sentence: States the main topic and controlling idea.
2. Supporting Sentences: Provide explanations, facts, statistics, or examples.
3. Concluding Sentence: Summarizes the main point or restates the topic sentence.

vocab_development.rules: Suffixes -tion and -sion convert verbs into abstract nouns (pollute -> pollution, prevent -> prevention, decide -> decision). Suffix -ness converts adjectives into nouns representing states (ill -> illness, fit -> fitness, happy -> happiness, dark -> darkness).
examples: prevent -> prevention
fit -> fitness
happy -> happiness

see_also.rules: In conditional sentences, there is a slight pause and rising intonation at the end of the if-clause when it comes first, followed by a falling intonation at the end of the main clause.

grammar_details.focus: Conditionals with Modals/Imperatives & Infinitives of Purpose

rules.usage: Explaining the reason or purpose for doing an action.
examples: Tourists travel to Isfahan to see famous tilework.
He went to the bazaar to buy a handcrafted carpet.

rules.structure: Conditional Type 1 with Imperatives or Modals
rules.formula: If + Simple Present, Imperative verb  |  If + Simple Present, modal + base verb
examples: If you visit Hamedan, visit the pottery workshops in Lalejin.
If we appreciate our heritage, we must preserve traditional crafts.

writing_skills.topic: Developing Supporting Sentences with Transition Words
rules: Supporting sentences explain the topic sentence using reasons, examples, or details.
Use transition words to connect ideas smoothly: 'for example', 'in fact', 'furthermore', 'therefore', 'in addition'.
Example: 'Persian art is world-famous. For example, handmade silk carpets from Isfahan are admired in international exhibitions.'

vocab_development.rules: Suffix -able means 'capable of being' (value -> valuable, enjoy -> enjoyable, accept -> acceptable, change -> changeable).
examples: value -> valuable
enjoy -> enjoyable
weave a carpet
make pottery

see_also.rules: Polite requests using modal verbs typically end with rising intonation (Could you show me that carpet, please?).

passages.title: Human Languages: Tools of Communication
passages.content: Language is a system of communication. People use language to share thoughts, feelings, and information. There are about seven thousand languages in the world today. Some languages have millions of native speakers, such as Chinese, Spanish, English, and Hindi. In small villages, only a few hundred people speak some endangered languages. Unfortunately, when older speakers pass away, some of these small languages may die out. Deaf people communicate using sign languages. Every country has its own sign language with special hand gestures, facial expressions, and symbols. Learning a foreign language helps us understand other cultures and respect people from different continents.

passages.title: Learning a Foreign Language
passages.content: Sina is talking to Carlos, an exchange student from Spain. Sina: 'How long have you studied Persian, Carlos?' Carlos: 'I have studied it for two years. It has a beautiful poetic rhythm.' Sina: 'Was it difficult to communicate at first?' Carlos: 'A little, but practicing with native speakers helped me improve rapidly. Learning languages connects people across continents.'

passages.title: Having a Healthy Lifestyle
passages.content: Good health is the most valuable gift in human life. To have a healthy lifestyle, we need to pay attention to both physical and emotional well-being. Eating a balanced diet is the first step. We should consume fresh vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and dairy products while avoiding too much sugar, salt, and fast food. Regular physical exercise, like jogging, cycling, or swimming, strengthens the heart and lungs. Spending too much time sitting and watching TV makes a person a couch potato and leads to weight gain. Managing daily stress, getting adequate sleep, and maintaining kind relationships with family and friends are equally important to prevent diseases.

passages.title: Consulting a Health Coach
passages.content: Coach: 'Reza, your health checkup shows you need more physical activity.' Reza: 'I study many hours a day and feel tired in the afternoon.' Coach: 'Avoid sitting for long hours. If you jog for thirty minutes every day and eat a balanced diet with fresh fruits, you will gain more energy and prevent heart illnesses.' Reza: 'Thank you coach, I will plan my daily routine right away.'

passages.title: Art and Culture in Iran
passages.content: Art is a mirror of a nation's culture, history, and spiritual values. Iran has one of the richest art heritages in the world. For thousands of years, Iranian artists and craftspeople have created magnificent works of art. Persian carpets are famous worldwide for their intricate patterns, natural colors, and high quality of weaving. Calligraphy is another respected art in Islamic culture. Skilled calligraphers use bamboo pens and ink to write poems of Hafez and verses of the Holy Quran. Pottery, tilework, miniature painting, and metalwork are other traditional crafts passed down through generations. These handmade arts show the patience, love, and creativity of Iranian people.

passages.title: Visiting an Art Exhibition in Isfahan
passages.content: Sara: 'Look at the vibrant colors of this silk carpet, teacher!' Art Teacher: 'Yes, skilled nomadic women wove this silk carpet using natural vegetable dyes.' Sara: 'Why is calligraphy so respected in Persian culture?' Art Teacher: 'Because calligraphers devoted their lives to writing holy texts and timeless wisdom. Each letter reflects deep balance, harmony, and spiritual beauty.'
